rows.description: A young adult asks a colleague or elder open questions about their path and listens without judging. Curiosity about others builds bonds and prevents stereotyping.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A child is satisfied with a simple toy and a good afternoon and does not compare it with others. Contentment at this age is fragile against advertisements and peers' possessions.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager who was fine with their phone or marks feels lacking after seeing friends' posts. Constant comparison manufactures dissatisfaction from nothing that has actually changed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young person who wants a bigger life is told to be satisfied with what the family has. Wanting more can coexist with gratitude, and blanket contentment can be a way of silencing dreams.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young professional enjoys the present and still pursues improvement without frantic urgency. This balance comes from valuing the process and not just the next rung.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A colleague notices a comfortable group repeating old methods and dismissing change. Success can breed complacency, and gentle questions about what is being missed can wake it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child cries when a favourite toy breaks or a blanket is washed away. Letting go is first practised with things, and honouring the loss briefly beats saying it is only a toy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child who has drifted from a close friend feels sad and disloyal. Friendships shifting is a normal experience, and space to mourn it helps the child move on.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager replays an old betrayal and refuses to forgive, feeling that forgiving means the harm did not matter. Letting go is a release for oneself and does not require reconciliation or approval of the act.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Letting go of an imagined future [Response]
rows.description: A student who missed a dream course mourns the life they pictured, then slowly builds interest in the path actually available. Grieving the planned future is part of making room for a real one.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
